chunks: The wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله would, if they had fasts due upon them, delay that until Shaʿban, disliking to prevent the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله from his need. And when Shaʿban came, they would fast, and he would fast with them.
And he عليه السلام used to say: “Shaʿban is my month.”

key_terms.حَاجَتَهُ: his need, referring here to the Prophet’s marital need
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: the month of Shaʿban, in which these fasts were made up
key_terms.شَهْرِي: my month, indicating the Prophet’s special association with Shaʿban
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَةَ: out of dislike or aversion to causing a hindrance

ai.seo_question: Why did the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله delay their make-up fasts until Shaʿban?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله would defer make-up fasting to Shaʿban so as not to hinder his marital needs. It also conveys the Prophet’s special association with the month of Shaʿban through his saying, “Shaʿban is my month.”

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1828 - It is narrated that the wives of the Prophet (sw) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), if they had missed obligatory fasts, would delay making them up until Sha‘ban, disliking to prevent the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) from fulfilling his needs. When Sha‘ban arrived, they would fast, and he would fast with them.
He (sw) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) used to say: "Sha‘ban is my month."
